kitDescription: Guilty: Mighty Bunny is a Water sniper who permanently gains 20.1% ATK and fights in one of two Bunny Modes. She opens the battle in Stance, which gives her +20.45% attack damage, +40% charge damage, and a 450.89% extra hit every time one of her full-charge shots lands. Holding a full charge for a second (outside her burst) flips her to Engage, where her normal shots and her burst attack become true damage and the per-shot extra hit becomes a 370.08% true-damage hit instead; flipping again returns her to Stance, and any teammate who also has a Bunny Mode is pulled into the same mode. Her Burst III swaps her to the Mighty Stomp weapon for exactly one round: a fixed 1.5-second charge, 101.3% damage with a 250% full-charge multiplier, boosted by +1400% charge damage for that single round, and she keeps +77.35% attack damage for 10 seconds afterwards.

redAssertions: VERBATIM RED, all one RECON_ERROR: the blind file assigns onEvent on the CompOptions top level (cfg.onEvent = ... where cfg is controlComp's return) but runComp only reads it under the nested cfg key (the driver's file uses cfg:{onEvent}), so the verbatim run captures ZERO events. The five event-reading assertions fail for that reason only: 'S1-a: ATK ▲20.1% is a plain self atkPct buff' (ap.length>0 on an empty log), 'S1-b: battle-start resolution is Stance' (no 20.45/40 buffApply seen), 'S2: exactly ONE Full-Charge rider fires' (shots.length>20 on an empty log), 'burst Add.1: ▲1400% is ROUND-scoped' (a.length>=2), 'burst Add.2: ▲77.35% TIME-scoped' (a.length>=2). The six totals-/structure-based assertions pass verbatim; three are the blind's own it.skip GAPs.

ADAPTED (one-line wiring fix only): 11 passed / 0 failed / 3 skipped — independently traced here against the driver's override: atkPct 20.1 self at frame 0 with no durationShots; 20.45 attackDamagePct + 40 chargeDamagePct on self by default (Stance); riders == charged shots (so > 5×bursts and within [shots−bursts−2, shots]); 1400 buffApplies each durationShots 1 and the durationSec-10 counterfactual strictly higher; 77.35 count == 1400 count, finite expiresFrame, no durationShots, durationSec-1 counterfactual lower. ZERO model divergences — the blind caught nothing against the shipped override.

gotchas.summary: Uses-based swap exit (maxShots 1) hands the base SR back with the swap-entry magazine minus the Stomp round, not the full magazine the 2026-08-12 real-weapon-change ruling describes for a swap exit; entry refills to her CURRENT max (9 with control-comp ammo buffs).
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Mighty Stomp: Changes the weapon in use … Duration: 1 rounds'. Driver caveat 3 documents it (⚑ estimate = full magazine less one per Stomp, footage recipe, MEASUREMENT-GATED). S6 caveat and S2b-2 note 4 independently flag swap shot economy as an always-⚑ item. Engine behaviour, not a prose divergence.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Needs measurement: in a focus recording read the ammo counter immediately before the burst cast, at the Stomp, and until the next reload; author the observed hand-back count (full / pre-cast / max−1) and, if the engine's uses-exit behaviour disagrees with the ruling, raise it as an engine item rather than patching this override.

gotchas.summary: The Stomp shot is routed as an ordinary SR normal attack: it cores at the flat 0.95 SR rate, takes the +30% range bonus in SR bands, and inherits SR burst-gauge value — none of which the kit states, and the driver's note does not record the convention.
gotchas.evidence: Kit names no weapon class for Mighty Stomp. §1b MG/SR/RL core = flat 0.95; swap inherits the base class. S6 flagged '⚑ Stomp core rate (default)' and 'weapon deliberately unset'; S2b-2 inertness line 'the Stomp never cores at a rate above the SR auto-core path (⚑ default)'. Driver: silent. At ~1712% × up to 6 casts the core term (+0.95 inside a Major of ~2.75) is a material share of one burst's payload.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Document the inherited-SR convention in the override note as ⚑, with the recipe: popup read of the Stomp on a focus recording (core-flavored vs body popups, and the ×1.3 range step across bands). If the Stomp proves core-ineligible, encode it as a non-coring hit (coreOverride 0 or a flatDamage delivery) — never tune the rate to a number.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA survives: all 13 kit lines are FAITHFUL (9) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (4: the mode toggle and the two ally-sync lines, verbatim in unmodeled with caveats). The two listed items are low: a documented ⚑ engine quirk on the uses-based swap exit magazine, and an undocumented but kit-silent convention that the Stomp cores/ranges as an SR shot (needs a popup read, not a value change). Every modeled block fires at prose cadence by the driver's event-log pins (ATK once at frame 0; ~100+ riders frame-locked to charged shots including the Stomp; one Stomp, one 1400-for-1-round and one 77.35-for-600f per own cast with helm's rotations correctly excluded), and every load-bearing assertion has a named counterfactual that diverges (mode-blind, unswapped-only rider, plain rider, no trueNormalsModes, no maxShots, 1.0s charge, 2-round 1400, all-allies 77.35; the durationSec misreads on 1400 are caught by G7's exact multiplier read). The blind re-derivations converged fully: S6's override is block-equivalent (passive vs battleStart, redundant crit:true under the SSOT default, non-binding durationSec 10, levelConst cosmetics), both S2b specs match the driver line-for-line, and the S5 test file is verbatim RED only because it wires onEvent where runComp never reads it (a harness RECON_ERROR); with that one line fixed it is 11/0/3 against the shipped override, independently traced here. Same-model residuals the owner should spot-check: (1) every agent read 'when landing a Full Charge attack' as also firing on the Stomp pull — literal but unmeasured, ~6 extra riders per fight; (2) rider crit relies on the engine default and is not pinned by the driver's tests; (3) selecting Engage is strictly worse in-engine than Stance unless an ally grants True Damage ▲ (true damage's DEF bypass is ≈0.1% here), so the chart number is a Stance number — say so when reading it; (4) the Stomp core/range convention above.
